:::{#def-complex-number}
#### Complex number

A **complex number** is a number of the form

$$z = a + b\,i,$$

where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers and $i$ is the imaginary unit (@def-imaginary-unit).

- The **real part** of $z$ is $\operatorname{Re} z \eqdef a$.
- The **imaginary part** of $z$ is $\operatorname{Im} z \eqdef b$.
- The set of all complex numbers is $\mathbb{C} \eqdef \{a + b\,i : a, b \in \reals\}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{.definition}

Two complex numbers are equal exactly when their real parts are equal and their imaginary parts are equal.
A real number $a$ is the complex number $a + 0\,i$,
so $\reals$ is a subset of $\mathbb{C}$.

:::

::: notes
@axler2024linear [Definition 1.1, p. 2] defines $\mathbb{C}$ as the set of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ of real numbers, written $a + bi$,
and @axler2024linear [Definition 4.1, p. 120] defines the real and imaginary parts.
:::
